text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- The United Nations Development Programme will provide nearly $1.3 million to facilitate Vietnam's integration into the World Trade Organisation. About $400,000 of the fund comes from the government of Switzerland.
-- An international consortium is expected to be named on Sunday to develop a special economic zone with deep-sea port and satellite city on a man-made peninsula in the Tonkin Gulf.
-- Vietnam and Australia have approved the final design for the construction of a $74 million bridge spanning the Mekong River at My Thuan.

-- A workshop to prepare for Vietnam's first national conference to discuss cooperation between the government and non-governmental organisations in population and development was held in Hanoi on Wednesday.
-- Belgium's Deputy Prime Minister, Minister of Finance and Foreign Trade Philippe Maystadt will arrive on Saturday for a four-day official visit to Vietnam.

-- The provincial Planning and Investment Service has suggested that Da Nang Beer and Soft Drink Factory buy out the foreign stake in BGI-Danang held by French brewer Brasseries et Glacieres Internationales (BGI), if the foreign partner decides to withdraw from the project, the Dau Tu newspaper said.
-- Do Muoi, Secretary General of the Communist Party, has called for improved efforts by the Party Control Commission and strengthening of the Party leadership in all socio-economic fields.
-- Vietnam has completed the first stage of installation of two main internet gateways in Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City.
-- A $13.78-million joint venture has been established to manufacture motorbike parts for Honda Motor Company. The factory is expected to start operation in 1997.
-- Construction of the $80 million My Thuan Bridge, the biggest in the Mekong delta, is planned to start in June, 1997.
